result.synthesis:
# Subfunction Classification Report

## 1. Task-shared, fully generic
Safe to treat as unified; never branch per-task. All variation enters via the `P` struct or `outDat` labels, not code.

| Function | Notes |
|---|---|
| `downsample_data` | Only branch is data dimensionality (2D/3D). Hardcoded filter design, but nothing varies by task. |
| `preprocess_eeg` | Fully task-agnostic; only runtime branch is data-driven good-channel count. `P` accepted but unused. |
| `preprocess_macros` | No in-body task branch; behavior carried by `P.spikeClean`. Task gating lives at call sites. |
| `preprocess_respiration_wholetrace` | Channel pick driven by `'rsp'` label + `rspIDX`/`rspFlip`. Already clean. |
| `detect_sniffs_from_TTLs` | No in-body branch; per-task TTL shaping happens in callers (esp. thresh rebuild). |
| `refine_onsets_with_phase` | Only `P.adjWin` varies. `P.task` unused. |
| `detect_spikes` | Fully generic; task-specific thresh/win passed by callers. |
| `plot_sniff_epochs` | Identical call everywhere; pure diagnostics. |
| `parSave` | Pure save wrapper; zero branching. |

## 2. Contain task-specific branches
Functions with real condition/task branching inside the body.

| Function | Branch(es) | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| `process_respiration_breathing` | `if ismember('cyclicSigh', behDat.cndName)` merges consecutive inhales; guarded by presence of `cndName` column; relies on breathing-only `.behDat`/`.TTL`. | **Split.** Isolate the cyclicSigh merge into a clearly-named local subfunction (`mergeCyclicSighBreaths`). The else branch is a dead no-op — delete. Channel-select/flip/`breathTemplates4` are generic and can stay outside the branch. |
| `flagBadBreaths` | `strcmp(behDat.task,'cyclicSigh')` force-accepts those breaths regardless of shape. | **Mark, don't split.** Single one-line condition-name exception; keep inline with a comment. Function is otherwise breathing-only by call site. |
| `alignTargetBreathingTraceSimplify` | Multiple: `cndName` presence (else `startFrom=3`), `'pre'`/`'audio'` baseline zero-fill, `{fastFocus,slowFocus,naturalFocus}` focus zero-fill, and the core `shadowFile ∈ {audioResp,focusedResp}` split selecting **two distinct alignment algorithms** (+`'NA'`→`audioResp` remap, sessID-skip at call site). | **Split the two algorithms** into `buildTarget_direct` vs `buildTarget_tempoLoop` subfunctions; hoist shared CSV-load + plotting out of the branch. This is the densest task-specific logic of the set. |
| `outMat_to_table` | No code branch on task, but the special remap keys on `'response'`@5 + `'response_str'`@6 (cueTask schema) with magic `999` sentinel and `6:8→7:9` shift. | **Treat as cueTask-specific** (Section 3). Keep as-is; it degrades safely to plain `cell2table` for other layouts. |

`build_behavior_table_{cueTask,threshTask,O15}` carry hardcoded `sniffTypes`/`trialTypes` vocab and per-task `rawBeh` field names — these are *task selection by filename*, not in-body routers (see Section 3 + 4).

## 3. Task-specific by nature
Each used by exactly one task; belong wholly inside that task's section.

| Function | Task | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `process_respiration_breathing` | breathing | Per-breath metric matrix + cyclicSigh merge |
| `processECG` | breathing | HRV / beat detection (despite being listed "shared") |
| `flagBadBreaths` | breathing | Per-breath QC |
| `alignTargetBreathingTraceSimplify` | breathing | Shadow/paced target-trace alignment |
| `build_behavior_table_breathingTask` | breathing | Per-breath behavior table |
| `plotBreathLengths` | breathing | QC heatmaps |
| `build_behavior_table_cueTask` | cueTask | Per-sniff table (`{"cued"}`) |
| `outMat_to_table` | cueTask | Behavioral cell→table normalization |
| `build_behavior_table_threshTask` | threshTask | Per-sniff table (`{air,low,med}`) |
| `build_behavior_table_O15` | O15 | Per-sniff table (`{start,free,confirm}`) |
| `detect_ttls_O15` | O15 | Photodiode→TTL parser; entire body encodes O15 geometry |

Note: `processECG`, `flagBadBreaths`, `plotBreathLengths`, `plot_sniff_epochs` have task-agnostic bodies but `processECG`/`flagBadBreaths`/`plotBreathLengths` are called only from `breathingTaskPreProc_main.m`, so they are de-facto breathing-only.

## 4. Redundancy / simplification opportunities

**Highest-value (cross-function duplication):**
- **`build_behavior_table_*` ×4 (+EmotionalMovie)** are near-identical: same first 6 columns from `sniffs` cols `1,2,3,4,6,6`, same `sniffLabel` mapping, same nested `find(behDat.n==ii)` broadcast loop. Only `sniffTypes`/`trialTypes` vocab and the `rawBeh` field list differ. **Factor into one generic builder** taking a task spec (sniffType labels + field map); leave only the vocab as the task-specific stub. The double loop is also an inefficient element-by-element grow — vectorize with logical indexing.
- **`parSave` / `parSaveClean`** are identical except saved var name — collapse into one helper with an optional var-name arg.

**Dead / commented code to delete:**
- `detect_spikes` lines ~178-241: entire legacy per-sample loop, commented out.
- `process_respiration_breathing`: dead else branch (computes `startIdx/endIdx`, used only in commented code); live `figure/hold/plot` will pop a figure per cyclicSigh segment in batch runs — remove or gate.
- `alignTargetBreathingTraceSimplify`: unreachable `error(...)`+`continue`, multiple commented plotting blocks, stale docstring (`codePre` arg doesn't exist).
- `preprocess_macros`: commented butter/gammaSig lines; `preprocess_eeg`: commented `ephysDat`/blinkIndicator append lines.
- `outMat_to_table`: `isEmptyValue` re-runs `isempty` in an unreachable char branch (no-op).

**Within-function duplication to hoist:**
- `detect_spikes`: positive- vs negative-spike blocks are mirror copy-paste → one helper called twice.
- `preprocess_macros`: two near-identical macro-raw plotting blocks (full vs zoom); `idx`/`macroDat` recomputed 3×; spikeClean true/false branches duplicate the channel-append + `spikeRemoval=1` tail.
- `preprocess_eeg`: the two arms of the `>10 good chans` branch repeat badChans/append/flag bookkeeping → factor shared appends out.
- `alignTargetBreathingTraceSimplify`: CSV-load block and plotting block copy-pasted across both shadowFile branches.
- `detect_sniffs_from_TTLs`: cued vs free threshold-crossing `find(...)` nearly identical → one helper `(startSearch,endSearch,firstOnly)`.
- `refine_onsets_with_phase`: fallback zero-crossing `find()` recomputes line-45 expression; three skip branches duplicate `adjust=0; finalOnset=s0; continue`.
- `plotBreathLengths`: `idx` and `[~,order]=sort` recomputed identically; two imagesc blocks near-identical.

**Latent bugs / correctness flags (surface before simplifying):**
- **`flagBadBreaths`**: the bad-breath branch indexes the **full** `rrDat` by `bonset:boffset` (recording's opening seconds) instead of `curRR` — likely a bug; both branches probably intended `curRR`. The duplicated RR min/max block should be hoisted and computed once from `curRR`.
- **`detect_ttls_O15`**: warm-up trim loop has commented-out `break`, so it keeps the **last** qualifying index, not the first; `ups` is not trimmed in parallel with `downs/difVals`, falling out of alignment (unused afterward, but fragile).
- **`preprocess_macros`**: `P.spikeThresh` is in the schema/P-struct but **never used** — `detect_spikes` is called with a hardcoded literal `2`. Per-session `spikeThresh` values currently have no effect (wiring appears lost). Decide: wire it in or drop from schema.
- **`detect_spikes`**: header claims `winSize` default 5 but no default is assigned → errors if called with 2 args.
- **`plotBreathLengths`**: RRint plot reuses the rsp x-axis vector `-2:.002:14` (8001 pts) for a 6001-sample window → mislabeled heart-rate axis.
- **`plot_sniff_epochs`** / `refine_onsets_with_phase`: comments say "-1 s to +2 s" / window docs but code uses ±2/+4 s — fix comments.

**Parameterization candidates (magic numbers to surface):**
- `preprocess_eeg`: the `32` channel count, exempt `[1 32]`, `>10` good-chan threshold.
- `preprocess_macros`: hardcoded 6-macro assumption (`ii=2:6`, 5 bipolar names) — will error/mislabel for ≠6 macros.
- `preprocess_respiration_wholetrace`: smoothing window `500` (×3), clip `10000`, `1 Hz` lowpass.
- `detect_sniffs_from_TTLs`: duplicated window offsets `30/1000/300/2000` between search setup and offset bookkeeping.
- `detect_ttls_O15`: `nan(15,20)`, `30`, `3500`, and the 20 one-by-one `free*` column assignments → build via loop/array.

found.name: downsample_data
found.inputs: outDat (struct with .data [ch x time OR ch x time x trials], .fs scalar, optionally .tim); fs_new (target sample rate scalar, e.g. 500).
found.outputs: outDat with .data resampled+filtered, .fs=fs_new, plus new fields .origFS (old fs), .downsampled=1, and .tim recomputed if it already existed. 2D input returns 2D; 3D input returns 3D.
found.purpose: Resamples and cleans a multichannel (and optionally multi-trial) signal to a new sample rate. It computes rational resample factors via rat(fs_new/fs_old), normalizes input to a 3D ch x time x trials array, and loops over every channel and trial: resample(p,q), then filtfilt with a 4th-order 0.03 Hz IIR highpass, a 4th-order lowpass at the new Nyquist minus 0.1 Hz, then three iirnotch filters at 60/120/180 Hz line noise (each Q=35). It restores the original 2D shape when input was 2D and updates the struct's fs/origFS/downsampled/tim bookkeeping fields. The filter objects (highd/lowd) are designed once before the loop, but the three notch filters are recomputed identically on every channel/trial iteration.
found.redundancyNotes: Fully task-agnostic: no branching on task, sessID, Type, or any task-specific channel/field names. Only branching is on data dimensionality (ndims==2 vs ==3, with an error for anything else) — structural, not task-specific. Redundancy/dead-code worth flagging for the simplify pass: (1) the three iirnotch designs (wo/bw/[b,a]=iirnotch) are inside the per-channel, per-trial double loop but depend only on fs_new — they should be hoisted out and computed once alongside highd/lowd. (2) double() is applied redundantly: sig is already cast via double(squeeze(...)) at the top of the loop, yet double(sig) is repeated in each notch filtfilt call. (3) The misleading copy-paste comments \"% transpose to filter along time\" — no transpose actually happens (filtfilt operates column-wise but sig is a row vector; works because resample/filtfilt handle vectors regardless of orientation). (4) Blank/no-op lines (the empty body after `for ii = 1:ch`, stray blank lines 70-73). None of this affects correctness; all are pure simplification opportunities. Note the filter design (0.03 Hz highpass, line-noise notches, no per-channel options) is hardcoded — if any task ever needs different filtering this is where a parameter would enter, but currently nothing varies by task.

found.name: preprocess_eeg
found.inputs: outDat (session struct: requires .labels, .data with first 32 rows = scalp EEG, .fs, .sessID), standardEEGlocs (table from EEG-coords CSV: .Label, .phi_deg, .theta_deg, .X_nose_m, .Y_left_m, .Z_up_m, .X2D_right, .Y2D_front), and P (the per-session param struct). NOTE: P is accepted in the signature but is NEVER referenced anywhere in the body.
found.outputs: outDat with added/modified fields: .eegLocs (table of labels+3D/2D coords+theta/phi), cleaned .data(1:32,:), appended rows + labels for blinkIndicator/badTS/interpChan, .badChans, .dataLap, .dataLapFromInterp, .EEGInterpolation, .EEGCleaning, .blinkRemoval.
found.purpose: Shared (task-agnostic) scalp-EEG cleaning stage in the 4-task preprocessing pipeline. It first validates that the first 32 channels of outDat.labels exactly match standardEEGlocs.Label (errors out otherwise), then builds an eegLocs coordinate table from the standard-locs CSV. It runs voltage-based noise/bad-channel detection and epoch interpolation (removeNoiseChansVolt), exempting channels 1 and 32 from being flagged bad. If more than 10 good channels survive, it performs blink removal (blinkRemoveWrapper), accumulates bad channels, computes a surface Laplacian (laplacian_perrinX) on a temporary copy in which bad channels are interpolated (interpolate_perrinX) so the spatial high-pass is not corrupted, writes the blink-cleaned broadband data back to outDat.data(1:32,:) keeping real values at bad sites, and appends blinkIndicator/badTS/interpChan as extra data rows with matching labels (sets EEGInterpolation=EEGCleaning=blinkRemoval=1, dataLapFromInterp=1). If 10 or fewer good channels remain, it skips blink removal and Laplacian (dataLap=[], dataLapFromInterp=0, blinkRemoval=0), appends only badTS/interpChan, and still sets EEGInterpolation=EEGCleaning=1. Called only when P.hasEEG is true at each call site.
found.redundancyNotes: 1) Unused parameter: P is in the signature but never used in the body; either wire it in (e.g. for the magic constants below) or drop it for clarity. 2) Hard-coded magic numbers that are good candidates to centralize/parameterize for the 'simplify' goal: the 32-channel count (loop `for chan=1:32`, indices `1:32`, `[1 32]`), the EXEMPT channels `[1 32]`, and the `length(chanIDX) > 10` good-channel threshold gating blink removal/Laplacian. 3) Duplicated tail code: the two arms of the `if length(chanIDX) > 10 ... else ... end` block repeat nearly identical bookkeeping (computing badChans/labels, appending badTS+interpChan rows, setting EEGInterpolation=EEGCleaning=1); only the blink/Laplacian portion and three flag/field values actually differ, so the shared appends could be factored out of the branch. 4) Commented-out dead lines remain in the else-branch (the `ephysDat`/blinkIndicator append lines). 5) The label-mismatch check `error('EEG channels not labeled as expected')` is a hard stop with no per-task context. NONE of these are task-specific — the function is fully task-agnostic; the only runtime branch is the data-driven good-channel-count test, not any task/sessID/Type/channel-name switch.

found.purpose: Extracts the respiration channel from outDat.data (rows whose label contains 'rsp'), selects the P.rspIDX-th respiration row, applies the P.rspFlip sign, then runs breathTemplates4(rspDat, fs) to produce a per-breath metric matrix bmObj (onset/peak/end Y and time, length, amplitude, exhale peak, condition, index). found.name: preprocess_respiration_wholetrace
found.inputs: outDat struct. Reads: outDat.labels (cell of channel-label strings), outDat.data (channels x samples matrix), outDat.rspIDX (which respiration channel to pick among the 'rsp'-labeled rows), outDat.rspFlip (+1/-1 sign flip), outDat.fs (sampling rate).
found.outputs: R struct with 5 fields: R.rspDat (selected, flipped raw respiration trace), R.smoothR (Gaussian-smoothed trace), R.testSig (deflection-detection metric, named field 'testSig'), R.analytic (smoothed + lowpassed Hilbert analytic signal), R.rspPhase (instantaneous respiration phase = angle of analytic).
found.purpose: Computes a whole-trace respiration representation used by the non-breathing tasks (cue, thresh, O15) and also called in breathingTaskPreProc_main and emotionalMovie/scratch scripts. It (1) selects the respiration channel: finds rows whose label contains 'rsp', then indexes into that subset with outDat.rspIDX, and multiplies by outDat.rspFlip to orient the signal; (2) Gaussian-smooths the trace over ~0.6 s; (3) builds a "deflection detect" onset metric by taking a windowed (~0.06 s) squared difference times the smoothed signal, clipping to [0,10000], then smoothing (window 500); (4) computes the analytic signal via hilbert(), smooths it (window 500), lowpasses at 1 Hz, and takes the phase angle. Returns all intermediate signals plus the phase in R. The phase/onset outputs feed downstream onset refinement (refine_onsets_with_phase) and behavior-table building.
found.redundancyNotes: Function is fully task-agnostic: no switch/if on task, sessID, or Type, and no hard-coded task-specific channel/field names — channel selection is driven entirely by outDat.labels containing 'rsp' plus outDat.rspIDX/rspFlip, which are set per-session upstream (applyParams/assemble), so this is already a clean shared helper needing no task-specific section. Minor cleanup opportunities (non-task): (a) several magic numbers are hard-coded rather than derived from fs or named params — the smoothing window 500 (samples, used 3x), clip ceiling 10000, lowpass cutoff 1 Hz, the 0.6 s and 0.06 s window scalars; these are fs-implicit and would be clearer as named locals. (b) R.testSig is the deflection metric but the field name 'testSig' reads as scratch/debug naming inconsistent with the descriptive comment at call sites ('onset_metric'); consider renaming for clarity. (c) Trailing blank lines 31-39 are dead whitespace. (d) Note 'analytic' is smoothed along dim 1 then lowpassed on a complex signal — intentional but worth a comment. No duplicated logic or dead code branches.

found.name: detect_sniffs_from_TTLs
found.inputs: R: respiration-features struct from preprocess_respiration_wholetrace, used fields: R.testSig (1D signal threshold-crossed to find sniff onsets), R.smoothR (smoothed respiration, plotting only). P: param struct, used fields: P.cuedBackBuff, P.respThresh, P.fs_target. outDat: used fields: outDat.TTL (table; col1 trialStart, col2 buttonpress, col3:end sniff target indices), outDat.sessID (plot title), outDat.figs (output folder for per-trial jpgs).
found.outputs: outSniffs: a 30x7 numeric matrix (preallocated 30 rows, filled rows only). col1 = sniff onset index into data; col2 = trial number; col3 = sniff-within-trial number; col4 = offset from TTL; col6 = sniff type (1=start, 2=free, 3=confirm); col5 and col7 are left as zeros (col7 commented as "adjustment for phase align" but never written). Also writes one JPG per trial (sniffsTrialN.jpg) to outDat.figs as a side effect.
found.purpose: Given a per-trial table of TTL-marked sniff target indices, locates the actual respiration sniff-onset sample near each target by detecting upward threshold crossings of R.testSig past P.respThresh. It distinguishes three positional classes within each trial: the first target and the last target are treated as "cued" sniffs expected AFTER the TTL (type 1 = start, type 3 = confirm), searched in a window from target-30-cuedBackBuff to target+2000-30 (~4s), taking the first crossing. All middle targets are "free" sniffs expected BEFORE the TTL (type 2), searched from target-30-1000 to target-30+300 (~2s); when multiple crossings exist it picks the one with the largest local rise (testSig at +/-15 samples around each candidate). Found onsets are recorded with trial number, within-trial index, type, and an offset-from-TTL value (computed differently for free vs cued types). Finally it renders a diagnostic figure per trial overlaying smoothed respiration, TTL xlines, detected sniff xlines (green), and testSig on a right y-axis, saved as JPG.
found.redundancyNotes: The two threshold-crossing detections (cued branch lines 28-30 and free branch lines 42-44) are nearly identical `find(testSig(a:b-1)<thr & testSig(a+1:b)>thr)` expressions differing only in window bounds and whether the first vs all crossings are kept; could be factored into a single local helper taking (startSearch,endSearch,firstOnly). Two dead commented-out lines (45: val clamping; 50-52 region has live code but lines 45-46 commented). The offset computation in col4 (lines 74-78) hardcodes the same window-offset constants (-30-1000 for free, -30-cuedBackBuff for cued) that were already used to build startSearch above (lines 26,39,77 vs 39,75) — these magic offsets (30, 1000, 300, 2000) are duplicated between the search-window setup and the offset bookkeeping and between the two branches; consolidating window definitions would remove the duplication. The output is documented as having 7 columns and col7 is described ("adjustment for phase align") but col5 and col7 are never assigned.
